- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.4) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price > 10% above 30-day moving avg, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.6, -0.4, +0.6), model tends to lag; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to catch momentum.
